cases.think: The star of the sentence: who or what performs the action, or is described.

talk.en: muktiḥ: "liberation" is what is being defined.

cases.role: what is acted on, or where it reaches
cases.think: The action lands on it: the thing done to, or the place gone to.

talk.en: yamālayam: “to Yama’s abode”, the destination of the beings.

cases.role: the means or tool; the one accompanying
cases.q: by what? with what? with whom?
cases.think: The tool or route by which it happens. Also the agent of a passive verb.

talk.en: vittena: “by means of wealth”, no immortality comes by that route.

cases.think: The one who receives, or the goal something is for.

ex.en: Rāma gives fruit to a friend.

talk.en: puṇyāya: “for merit”, helping others leads to merit.

cases.role: the source; where it separates or comes from
cases.think: The starting point: the place, person or cause something moves away from.

talk.en: sakāśāt: “from the presence of” the teachers, the source of learning.

cases.role: of: a link between two nouns
cases.kar: not a kāraka (relates noun to noun)
cases.think: Belonging and relation: it joins one noun to another, not to the action.
The setting: where or when the action takes place.

talk.en: pṛthivyām: “on the earth”, where all people should learn.

cases.think: Not part of the action at all: you are calling someone.

talk.en: No vocative appears in his quoted verses. Yājñavalkya would say he maitreyi (“O Maitreyī!”).

sutra.gloss: The independent one (the one who acts on its own) is the kartṛ.
What the agent most wishes to reach is the karman.
The most effective means is the karaṇa.
The one whom the agent intends to reach through the object is the sampradāna.
The fixed point from which separation occurs is the apādāna.
The support or substrate is the adhikaraṇa.
The sixth case is used for the remainder: any relation that is not a kāraka. Later grammarians call this sambandha, “relation”.
In addressing someone, the first-case affixes are used too. So for Pāṇini the vocative is a use of the first case, not an eighth case.

tad.note: Pronouns have no vocative. Feminine forms differ (e.g. sā, tām, tayā) and are not shown.

yad.note: Pronouns have no vocative. Feminine forms differ (e.g. sā, tām, tayā) and are not shown. Before a vowel or voiced sound, yat is written yad.

kim.note: Pronouns have no vocative. Feminine forms differ (e.g. sā, tām, tayā) and are not shown.

idam.note: Pronouns have no vocative. Feminine forms differ (e.g. sā, tām, tayā) and are not shown. The enam/enau/enān forms are short, unstressed alternates.

etad.note: Pronouns have no vocative. Feminine forms differ (e.g. sā, tām, tayā) and are not shown.

asmad.note: Same for all genders. Forms after "/" (mā, me, nau, naḥ) are short, unstressed alternates. No vocative.

tvad.note: Same for all genders. Forms after "/" are short, unstressed alternates. No vocative.

ahan.note: The nominative is also seen as ahar. Day: ahan. The stem shortens (ahn-) before vowel endings.

mahat.note: Adjectives take the gender, case and number of the noun they describe. Feminine: mahatī.

kartr.pattern: ṛ-stem masculine (agent nouns in -tṛ, like kartṛ “doer”, dātṛ)
kartr.note: The stem strengthens: kartṛ → kartār- (strong), kart- (weak) before some endings. The word kartṛ is itself Pāṇini’s name for the agent.

matr.note: Almost the same as kartṛ; only the accusative plural differs (mātṝḥ).

rajan.pattern: n-stem masculine (rājan, “king”): the stem takes three shapes
rajan.note: Strong stem rājān- (nominative and accusative singular/dual, nominative plural). Middle stem rāja- (before bh- and s-). Weak stem rājñ- (before other vowel endings: a drops, jn → jñ). The nominative singular rājā is the “dictionary” form, not the stem. In compounds the stem often becomes a-stem, so mahā-rāja declines like deva.

naman.note: Same three stem shapes as rājan: nāmān- is not used, but nām- / nāman- / nāmn- appear.

balin.note: The suffix -in means “possessing”: bala (strength) → balin (one who has strength).

manas.note: The final -s shows as -ḥ at the end of a word and -o- before bh-: manobhiḥ.

vac.note: The final c turns into k or g depending on what follows: vāk, vāgbhiḥ. The speaker’s word vāg-vyāpāra (V1) is this stem.

bhagavat.pattern: vat-stem masculine (-vat / -mat = “having”, like bhagavat “fortunate, the Lord”)
bhagavat.note: Strong stem bhagavant- / weak stem bhagavat-. mahat (great) follows the same pattern.

kr_pres.note: The root changes shape: kar- (strong) and kur- (weak).

kr_opt.note: The optative expresses wish, possibility or "should".

vac_fut.note: In the verse the prefix pra- is added: pra-vakṣyāmi.

gam_pres.note: The root gam- becomes gaccha- before endings.

is_pres.note: The root iṣ- becomes iccha- before endings.

as_pres.note: Irregular: the a of the root drops in many forms (staḥ, santi).

as_opt.note: Here the root appears only as s-.

as_imp.note: Command, blessing or permission: "let it be".

siks_opt.note: Ātmanepada endings: the action is "for oneself".

n_m:agrajanman.pattern: n-stem masculine after a consonant cluster (like janman, ātman: no contraction)

pron_a:sva.pattern: pronominal adjective (sva), pronoun-like endings in dative/ablative/locative
pron_a:sva.note: Feminine forms follow the ā-stem pattern with pronoun-style endings, e.g. sarvasyai.

pron_a:sarva.pattern: pronominal adjective (sarva), pronoun-like endings in dative/ablative/locative
pron_a:sarva.note: Feminine forms follow the ā-stem pattern with pronoun-style endings, e.g. sarvasyai.

V1:0:1.note: sarva + -tra: the -tra ending makes "in/at" adverbs (tatra "there", atra "here").
V1:0:1.label: indeclinable

V1:0:2.use: in Bharatavarsha: the place where the action happens.
V1:0:2.label: Loc. sg. n.

V1:0:3.use: by us: with a "should be done" verb, the doer takes the instrumental.
V1:0:3.note: asmad = "we" (first-person pronoun). Here the case and the role differ: the doer (kartṛ) of a “should be done” verb is put in the instrumental, because the verb already expresses the object.
V1:0:3.label: Instr. pl.

V1:0:4.note: sarva + -dā: the -dā ending makes "at the time" adverbs (tadā "then", yadā "when").
V1:0:4.label: indeclinable

V1:0:5.use: by means of the language of the gods: the instrument.
V1:0:5.label: Instr. sg. f.

V1:0:6.use: dealings and so on: the thing that ought to be done (subject of the passive).
V1:0:6.note: Here the object (karman) takes the nominative, because the “should be done” form of the verb (kartavyam) is passive and expresses the object itself.
V1:0:6.label: Nom. sg. n.

V1:0:7.use: ought to be done: -tavya makes a "should be done" adjective from √kṛ.
V1:0:7.label: Nom. sg. n.

V1:1:0.use: therefore: "from that", i.e. for that reason.
V1:1:0.note: The ablative of tad is used as "therefore".
V1:1:0.label: Abl. sg. n.

V1:1:3.use: the work of speech: the thing being done (object).
V1:1:3.label: Acc. sg. m.

V1:1:4.use: in/with a mleccha tongue: the means.
V1:1:4.label: Instr. sg. f.

V1:1:5.use: I do: first person singular, present.
V1:1:5.label: laṭ 1sg.

V1:2:0.use: pardon: what is being begged (object of yācitvā).
V1:2:0.label: Acc. sg. f.

V1:2:1.note: √yāc + -tvā: the "having done" ending makes a gerund (absolutive). It never changes form.
V1:2:1.label: gerund

V2:0:0.note: Written puṇyatamā before a voiced sound (visarga drops).
V2:0:0.label: Nom. pl. m.

V2:0:2.use: like Maheśa: describes the same people.
V2:0:2.label: Nom. pl. m.

V2:0:3.use: who: the relative pronoun; links the clause to the people described.
V2:0:3.label: Nom. pl. m.

V3:0:0.use: this: first member of the compound etad-deśa-prasūta.
V3:0:0.note: In a compound, the first members appear in their bare stem form; only the last member takes the case ending. The ending on prasūtasya applies to the whole compound.

V3:0:1.use: land: second member of the compound.
V3:0:1.note: Bare stem inside a compound. Shown: how deśa declines on its own.

V3:0:2.use: of one born in this land: the genitive for the whole compound.
V3:0:2.note: prasūta = pra + √sū + -ta ("born"), a past participle. The compound qualifies agrajanmanaḥ.
V3:0:2.label: Gen. sg. m.

V3:0:3.use: from the presence of: the source one learns from.
V3:0:3.note: sakāśāt functions almost like a postposition "from".
V3:0:3.label: Abl. sg. m.

V3:0:4.use: of the foremost-born: whose presence it is.
V3:0:4.note: Genitive and ablative singular are spelled the same here. The sense is "of the foremost-born".
V3:0:4.label: Gen. sg. m.

V3:1:0.use: each their own: repeating a word means "each one’s".
V3:1:0.note: The repetition svaṁ svam means "each their own".
V3:1:0.label: Acc. sg. n.

V3:1:1.use: conduct: what is to be learned (object).
V3:1:1.label: Acc. sg. n.

V4:0:0.use: of all: relates the power to the words.
V4:0:0.label: Gen. pl. m.

V4:0:1.use: of words: whose power it is.
V4:0:1.label: Gen. pl. m.

V4:0:2.use: in their own meaning: where the power lies.
V4:0:2.label: Loc. sg. m.

V4:0:3.use: power: the subject of the statement.
V4:0:3.label: Nom. sg. f.

V5:0:0.use: obtainable: -ya makes a "can be obtained" adjective from √labh.
V5:0:0.label: Nom. sg. n.

V5:0:4.use: is / becomes: third person singular, present.
V5:0:4.label: laṭ 3sg.

V5:1:0.use: farming: first member of the compound.
V5:1:0.note: Bare stem inside a compound. Shown: how kṛṣi declines on its own.

V5:1:1.use: straw: second member of the compound.
V5:1:1.note: palāla: straw or chaff (it can be masculine or neuter). In the recording the ending is unclear, so no table is shown.
V5:1:1.label: compound member

V6:0:0.use: with half a verse: the means.
V6:0:0.note: ardha as "a half" in this kind of compound is neuter (Pāṇini 2.2.2).
V6:0:0.label: Instr. sg. n.

V6:0:1.use: I shall tell: first person singular, future.
V6:0:1.note: Full verse form: pra-vakṣyāmi (prefix pra- “forth”). The table shows the root without the prefix.
V6:0:1.label: lṛṭ 1sg.

V6:0:2.use: what: the thing that has been said.
V6:0:2.note: yat becomes yad before a vowel (yad uktam). The object (karman) takes the nominative because uktam (“said”) is a passive participle.
V6:0:2.label: Nom. sg. n.

V6:0:3.note: √vac + -ta, with the vowel change vac → uk.
V6:0:3.label: Nom. sg. n.

V6:0:4.use: by crores of books: who/what has said it (the agent of the passive).
V6:0:4.note: The agent (kartṛ) takes the instrumental because uktam is passive: “said by crores of books”.
V6:0:4.label: Instr. pl. f.

V6:1:1.use: for merit: the purpose or result.
V6:1:1.note: A dative of purpose (“for the sake of”), so Pāṇini’s sampradāna (recipient) does not apply strictly here.
V6:1:1.label: Dat. sg. n.

V6:1:2.use: for sin: the purpose or result.
V6:1:2.note: A dative of purpose (“for the sake of”), so Pāṇini’s sampradāna (recipient) does not apply strictly here.
V6:1:2.label: Dat. sg. n.

V6:1:3.use: hurting others: the subject of the second half.
V6:1:3.label: Nom. sg. n.

V7:0:0.use: liberation: the subject of the definition.
V7:0:0.label: Nom. sg. f.

V7:0:1.note: √hā + -tvā: hā becomes hi- before -tvā. Gerunds never change form.
V7:0:1.label: gerund

V7:0:2.use: the other forms: what is given up (object of hitvā).
V7:0:2.label: Acc. sg. n.

V7:0:3.use: in/by one’s own form: the state one rests in.
V7:0:3.note: ṇ: after r, the n of -ena turns into ṇ (rūpeṇa).
V7:0:3.label: Instr. sg. n.

V7:0:4.use: being established: second part of the definition.
V7:0:4.label: Nom. sg. f.

V8a:0:0.use: of immortality: what the hope concerns.
V8a:0:0.label: Gen. sg. n.

V8a:0:3.use: by means of wealth: the instrument.
V8a:0:3.note: vitta = "obtained", from √vid (to obtain). Here a neuter noun: wealth.
V8a:0:3.label: Instr. sg. n.

V8b:0:0.use: by which: the means through which one might become immortal.
V8b:0:0.label: Instr. sg. n.

V8b:0:3.use: I should be: first person optative.
V8b:0:3.label: vidhiliṅ 1sg.

V8b:0:5.use: with that: the thing I would use.
V8b:0:5.label: Instr. sg. n.

V8b:0:6.use: should I do: first person optative.
V8b:0:6.label: vidhiliṅ 1sg.

V9:0:2.note: √jīv + -ta: a past participle used as a noun, "lived-ness", life.
V9:0:2.label: Nom. sg. n.

V9:1:1.use: vehicles (horses, chariots): the things that are yours.
V9:1:1.label: Nom. pl. m.

V9:1:3.use: dance and song (two things): subject of the second half.
V9:1:3.note: Dual: exactly two things. The ending -e marks dual in the neuter nominative/accusative/vocative.
V9:1:3.label: Nom. du. n.

V10:0:0.use: on a day, repeated: "day after day".
V10:0:0.note: Repeating a word gives "each / every": ahany ahani, day after day.
V10:0:0.label: Loc. sg. n.

V10:0:1.note: bhūta = “become, been”: a past participle used as a noun for “beings”.
V10:0:1.label: Nom. pl. n.

V10:0:4.note: With verbs of going, the destination takes the accusative and counts as the karman.
V10:0:4.label: Acc. sg. m.

V10:1:1.use: the permanent state: what they wish for.
V10:1:1.note: sthāvara = “stationary”, from √sthā (to stand). Also seen as neuter.
V10:1:1.label: Acc. sg. m.

V10:1:4.use: a wonder: what is being asked about.
V10:1:4.label: Nom. sg. n.

multi.label: indeclinable
multi.note: param is actually the neuter singular of para (“other, beyond”) used as an adverb.

V12:0:0.use: Śrī Kṛṣṇa: first member of the compound.
V12:0:0.note: Bare stem inside a compound (śrī + kṛṣṇa). Shown: how kṛṣṇa declines on its own.

V12:0:1.use: an offering: the subject of "let it be".
V12:0:1.label: Nom. sg. n.
